cases.title: Departure from Paris
cases.intro: The Midnight Express has barely left the Gare de l'Est when a scream rings out. Mr. Thorne lies still, and you are the only detective aboard. Sir Sterling, the British diplomat, keeps one hand on a locked dispatch box.
cases.outro: Mr. Norcross is locked in the baggage car until the next station.

steps.text: Your first case. Every row and every column holds exactly one person, the victim included. Start with the victim: Mr. Thorne was standing under a lamp, and there is only one lamp on the board (row 2, column 1). Tap T below, then tap the lamp.

Mr. Thorne now owns row 2 and column 1, so nobody else can use them (they are shaded). Mr. Norcross was on the Platform, room 1 at the top left. Only one Platform cell is still free. Tap N, then tap that cell.
Conductor Czerny was standing on a rug. There are two rugs in row 4, but column 2 already belongs to Mr. Norcross. Tap C, then tap the other rug.
Madame Ortolan was in the Lounge Car (room 3). Rows 1, 2 and 4 are taken, so she is in row 3, in the only column nobody has yet. Tap O and place her.

tutorial.accuse: Everyone is in place. The murderer is the only person who was alone with the victim. Mr. Thorne is on the Platform with just one other person. Tap Accuse and name them.

cases.title: Arrival in Vienna
cases.intro: The lights of Vienna are in sight, and the piano in the lounge car has played the same four notes all evening. Mr. Jessop worked out what they meant, and paid for it.
cases.outro: Signor Moretti confesses on the Vienna platform: the four notes were a code, played for someone called the Nightjar. The target is the Star of the Bosphorus, a sapphire hidden in Sir Sterling's dispatch box. The Nightjar is still aboard.
